lines: Low frequency oscillator tracing a point around a circle whose radius bounces in and out, producing a pair of complex pulsing signals at its X and Y outputs
Sets how fast the point travels around the circle, -10 to 10 rotations per second, a negative value running the pattern the other way
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the speed, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the speed; every 1V here turns the SPEED knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Sets how many times the radius bounces in and out on each rotation, 1 to 17
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the ratio, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the ratio; every 1V here turns the RATIO knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
LOCK rounds the ratio to a whole number, so the pattern of accents repeats on every rotation; FREE allows fractional ratios, so the accents vary from one rotation to the next
Sets how far the radius bounces in from the outer edge, 0 to 100%, which sets how much the bounce dominates the output
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the depth, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the depth; every 1V here turns the DEPTH knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Offsets the phase of the bounce cycle, -180 to 180 degrees, which shifts where the accents fall in each rotation
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the phase offset, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the phase offset; every 1V here turns the PHASE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Scales that output from 0 to 200%, applied after the voltage range is chosen
Modulates the gain of that output; every 1V here turns the GAIN knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets the range of that output: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
The horizontal coordinate of the traced point, as a slow pulsing signal
The vertical coordinate of the traced point, as a slow pulsing signal
Note — patching X into a scope's X input and Y into its Y input, with the scope in X times Y mode, draws the flower-like shape the module traces
Generates one envelope stage, with a CV input for each knob, a choice of J or S curves, and a button beside each control jack
Sets the voltage at which the generated stage ends, within the range chosen by the UNI/BI switch
Sets the range of the LEVEL knob: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
Modulates the level; every 1V here turns the LEVEL knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets the curvature of the stage; centred is a straight line, clockwise pushes the steep part towards the end and counter-clockwise towards the start, and the extremes are nearly square
Chooses the shape of the stage: a J curve that steepens at one end, or an S curve that steepens through the middle
Modulates the curvature; every 1V here turns the CURVE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets how long the stage takes, within the range chosen by the 1/10/100 switch
Sets the range of the DURATION knob: 1ms to 1 second, 10ms to 10 seconds, or 100ms to 100 seconds, with the knob centred giving a tenth of the maximum
Modulates the duration; every 1V here turns the DURATION knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
While this gate is high the IN signal passes straight to OUT and any stage in progress is abandoned; it reads high above 1V
Holds the DEFER signal at 10V while pressed, so the IN signal passes straight to OUT
A rising edge starts a stage from the voltage at IN; a rise during a stage abandons it and starts a new one, and rises are ignored while DEFER is high; it reads high above 1V
Holds the TRIG signal at 10V while pressed, which starts a stage
The voltage a stage starts from, sampled when the trigger arrives, and passed straight to OUT while DEFER is high
Carries the generated stage, the IN voltage while DEFER is high, or the LEVEL voltage after a stage has completed
Carries 10V while a stage is being generated or while DEFER is high, and 0V otherwise
Forces the ACTIVE output to 10V while pressed
Carries a 1ms 10V pulse when a stage completes
Forces the EOC output to 10V while pressed
Note — a knob turned while a stage runs takes effect at once, and the new value applies to the remainder of that stage
Eight latching buttons, each with a momentary negate button and an output
Toggles that row's output between 10V and 0V
Inverts that row's output while held, so a row reading 10V drops to 0V and a row reading 0V rises to 10V
Carries 10V while that row's button is on and 0V while it is off, inverted while the row's negate button is held
Transforms its input with a cubic polynomial: a times x cubed, plus b times x squared, plus c times x, plus d
Sets how much of x cubed is added to the result, -2 to 2
Sets how much of x squared is added to the result, -2 to 2; it can produce a large DC offset
Sets how much of x is added to the result, -2 to 2, which makes it an attenuverter on the input
Adds a constant to the result, reaching -10 to 10V with the OUT gain at 100%; it can produce a large DC offset
Scales the input before the polynomial is applied, 0 to 200%; a 5V input at 100% gives an x of 1
Scales the result before it leaves the module, 0 to 200%
Modulates the amount of x cubed added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the amount of x squared added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the amount of x added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the constant added to the result; every 1V here turns its knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the input gain; every 1V here turns the IN knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Modulates the output gain; every 1V here turns the OUT knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
The signal to transform, scaled by the IN gain knob to give x
The transformed signal, which can run far outside -5 to 5V; use the IN and OUT gain knobs to keep an audio signal in range
Cubic.notes: No family for the IN and OUT jacks: Cubic is a general transfer function, and the maker's own guide describes it as useful for both modulation signals and audio, so what those jacks carry depends on the patch.

lines: Generates a sequence of 4 envelope stages, each with its own mode, level, curve and duration; it is hidden from the module browser, and Sequencizer replaces it
Toggles the sequencer between running and paused; a sequence paused this way resumes from where it stopped
While this gate is high the sequencer runs, and while it is low a sequence in progress pauses where it is; it reads high above 1V
Toggles looping; with it on the sequencer begins a new sequence as soon as one ends, and with it off the sequencer goes idle
While this gate is high the sequencer begins a new sequence as soon as one ends; it reads high above 1V
Sets the step the sequence begins at
Sets how many steps the sequence runs for, counting on from the start step and wrapping round to step 1
Sends a gate for as long as it is held: from idle it starts the sequence, and the steps read it for their advance condition
Starts the sequence when it rises while the sequencer is idle, and the steps read it for their advance condition; it reads high above 1V
Abandons any paused or running sequence while pressed, leaving the sequencer idle
A rising edge abandons any paused or running sequence and leaves the sequencer idle
The input signal: a step in INPUT mode passes it to OUT, a step in CHASE mode curves towards it, and while RESET is high and the sequencer idle it is copied to OUT
Carries the voltage generated by the active step, or 0V before the first sequence
Chooses what that step generates: a curve to its LEVEL voltage, a hold at the current voltage, a sustain until it advances, the IN signal passed through, a curve chasing IN, or the LEVEL voltage
Chooses what advances the sequence past that step: TIME when the step's duration runs out, or the GATE rising, falling, either rising or falling, being high, or being low
Sets the voltage that step's curve ends at, within the range chosen by the level range switch
Chooses the shape of that step's curve: a J curve that steepens at one end, or an S curve that steepens through the middle
Sets the curvature of that step's curve; centred is a straight line, clockwise pushes the steep part towards the end and counter-clockwise towards the start, and the extremes are nearly square
Sets how long that step lasts, within the range chosen by the duration range switch
Enables that step; with it off the sequencer skips the step when advancing
While this gate is high that step is enabled, and the step is also enabled while its own button is on; it reads high above 1V
Sets the range of every step's LEVEL knob: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
Sets the range of every step's DURATION knob: 1ms to 1 second, 10ms to 10 seconds, or 100ms to 100 seconds, with the knob centred giving a tenth of the maximum
Note — the light above each step shows how far that step has progressed, running from red at the start of a timed step to green at its end
CurveSequencer4.notes: The last parameter has no name and no control on the panel: the source calls it GenerateModeMenu and nothing reads it, so it is left untagged.

lines: Combines two pairs of signals with fuzzy logic operators built from hyperbolic paraboloids, reading each voltage as a degree of truth
One of the two signals the A and B operators combine; its voltage is read as a degree of truth, completely false at the bottom of the chosen range and completely true at the top
One of the two signals the C and D operators combine; its voltage is read as a degree of truth, completely false at the bottom of the chosen range and completely true at the top
Negates that input before the operators are applied, turning complete truth into complete falsehood
Chooses the voltage range the operators are well behaved over; outside it the outputs can grow very large. It is -5 to 5V at UNI and 0-10V at BI, the opposite way round from the panel and the manual
The fuzzy AND of A and B: the two voltages multiplied together and divided by 10
The negation of the fuzzy AND of A and B
The fuzzy OR of A and B: their sum less their fuzzy AND
The negation of the fuzzy OR of A and B
The fuzzy XOR of A and B: their fuzzy OR less their fuzzy AND
The negation of the fuzzy XOR of A and B
The fuzzy implication from A to B: A negated, plus the fuzzy AND of the two
The negation of the fuzzy implication from A to B
The fuzzy implication from B to A: B negated, plus the fuzzy AND of the two
The negation of the fuzzy implication from B to A
The fuzzy AND of C and D: the two voltages multiplied together and divided by 10
The negation of the fuzzy AND of C and D
The fuzzy OR of C and D: their sum less their fuzzy AND
The negation of the fuzzy OR of C and D
The fuzzy XOR of C and D: their fuzzy OR less their fuzzy AND
The negation of the fuzzy XOR of C and D
The fuzzy implication from C to D: C negated, plus the fuzzy AND of the two
The negation of the fuzzy implication from C to D
The fuzzy implication from D to C: D negated, plus the fuzzy AND of the two
The negation of the fuzzy implication from D to C
FuzzyLogicH.notes: The UNI/BI switch looks inverted in the 2.0.3 source: the module adds a 5V offset to its inputs and subtracts it from its outputs when the switch is at UNI, which is the shift a bipolar signal needs rather than a unipolar one. The line follows the source and says that it contradicts the panel and the manual.

lines: Combines two pairs of signals with the fuzzy logic operators defined by Lofti Zadeh, reading each voltage as a degree of truth
One of the two signals the A and B operators combine; its voltage is read as a degree of truth, completely false at the bottom of the chosen range and completely true at the top
One of the two signals the C and D operators combine; its voltage is read as a degree of truth, completely false at the bottom of the chosen range and completely true at the top
Negates that input before the operators are applied, turning complete truth into complete falsehood
Chooses the voltage range the operators are well behaved over; outside it the outputs can grow very large. It is -5 to 5V at UNI and 0-10V at BI, the opposite way round from the panel and the manual
The fuzzy AND of A and B: the lesser of the two voltages
The negation of the fuzzy AND of A and B
The fuzzy OR of A and B: the greater of the two voltages
The negation of the fuzzy OR of A and B
The fuzzy XOR of A and B: the greater of the two voltages minus the lesser
The negation of the fuzzy XOR of A and B
The fuzzy implication from A to B: the greater of A negated and B
The negation of the fuzzy implication from A to B
The fuzzy implication from B to A: the greater of A and B negated
The negation of the fuzzy implication from B to A
The fuzzy AND of C and D: the lesser of the two voltages
The negation of the fuzzy AND of C and D
The fuzzy OR of C and D: the greater of the two voltages
The negation of the fuzzy OR of C and D
The fuzzy XOR of C and D: the greater of the two voltages minus the lesser
The negation of the fuzzy XOR of C and D
The fuzzy implication from C to D: the greater of C negated and D
The negation of the fuzzy implication from C to D
The fuzzy implication from D to C: the greater of C and D negated
The negation of the fuzzy implication from D to C

The line follows the source and says that it contradicts the panel and the manual.

lines: A knob with a selectable range that offsets or scales its input signal
Sets the amount added to or multiplied by the input, within the range currently chosen
Chooses the function applied to the input: ADD offsets it by adding the knob's voltage, MULT scales it by multiplying by the knob's value. Each function has its own set of knob ranges
Cycles the range of the knob while ADD is chosen: 0-5V, -5 to 5V, 0-10V or -10 to 10V
Cycles the range of the knob while MULT is chosen: 0 to 1, -1 to 1, 0 to 2, -2 to 2, 0 to 5, -5 to 5, 0 to 10, or -10 to 10
The signal the function is applied to; with nothing patched the function works on 0V
The input after the chosen offset or scaling
Func.notes: No family for the IN and OUT jacks: Func offsets or scales whatever it is given, so what those jacks carry depends on the patch.

lines: Six chained knobs with selectable ranges, each offsetting or scaling a signal
Sets the amount added to or multiplied by that channel's input, within the range currently chosen
Chooses the function applied to the input: ADD offsets it by adding the knob's voltage, MULT scales it by multiplying by the knob's value. Each function has its own set of knob ranges
Cycles the range of the knob while ADD is chosen: 0-5V, -5 to 5V, 0-10V or -10 to 10V
Cycles the range of the knob while MULT is chosen: 0 to 1, -1 to 1, 0 to 2, -2 to 2, 0 to 5, -5 to 5, 0 to 10, or -10 to 10
The signal that channel's function is applied to; with nothing patched it takes the output of the channel above, and the top channel takes 0V
That channel's input after its offset or scaling, and the signal the channel below takes when its own input is unpatched
Func6.notes: No family for the channel jacks: Func 6 offsets or scales whatever it is given, so what those jacks carry depends on the patch.

lines: Computes eight logic functions over as many as 16 inputs, counting only the inputs that are patched
Inverts that input before the logic functions are computed
One of the logic inputs; only patched inputs are counted, and a voltage above 1V counts as true, despite the manual giving the threshold as 0.5V
Carries 10V while every patched input is true, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while at least one patched input is false, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while at least one patched input is true, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while every patched input is false, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the number of true inputs is even, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the number of true inputs is odd, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while exactly one input is true, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the number of true inputs is anything other than one, and 0V otherwise
Note — with no input patched at all, every output carries 0V
Gator.notes: The maker's manual says an input above 0.5V counts as true; the 2.0.3 source reads an input as high above 1V. The line follows the source.

lines: Generates a hold or sustain envelope stage at the voltage it samples from IN
Chooses what the stage does: HOLD keeps the sampled voltage for the set duration, SUSTAIN keeps it until the GATE falls
Sets how long a hold stage lasts, within the range chosen by the 1/10/100 switch; a sustain stage ignores it
Sets the range of the DURATION knob: 1ms to 1 second, 10ms to 10 seconds, or 100ms to 100 seconds, with the knob centred giving a tenth of the maximum
Modulates the duration; every 1V here turns the DURATION knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
While this gate is high the IN signal passes straight to OUT, incoming gates are ignored, and any stage in progress is abandoned; it reads high above 1V
Triggers a hold stage, or holds a sustain stage up for as long as it stays high; it is ignored while DEFER is high, and it reads high above 1V
The voltage a stage holds, sampled when the stage starts, and passed straight to OUT while DEFER is high
Carries 10V while a stage is being generated or while DEFER is high, and 0V otherwise
Carries a 1ms 10V pulse when a stage completes
Carries the held voltage, or the IN voltage while DEFER is high
Note — before the module first becomes active it emits 0V, and changing the mode abandons any stage in progress
A knob whose two end points are themselves knobs, giving any voltage between them
Picks a point between the CCW and CW voltages, 0 to 100%
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the level, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the level; every 1V here turns the LEVEL knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter

Carries the voltage the LEVEL knob picks between the CCW and CW voltages
Note — control voltage can drive any of these knobs past its normal limit, so the output can leave the range the CCW and CW knobs describe
A scanned sequencer of 4 steps: a phase signal sweeps across the steps, and each step interpolates along a curve between two anchor voltages
Sets how many of the steps the sweep runs across
Sets the range of every anchor LEVEL knob: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI

Modulates that step's phase 1 level; every 1V here turns the LEVEL knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Chooses the shape of that step's curve: a J curve that steepens at one end, or an S curve that steepens through the middle
Sets the curvature of that step's curve; centred is a straight line, clockwise pushes the steep part towards the end and counter-clockwise towards the start, and the extremes are nearly square
Modulates that step's curvature; every 1V here turns the CURVE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets how much of the sweep that step takes up against the other steps, 0 to 200%; at 0 the step is skipped, and with every step at 0 the sequence stops
Modulates that step's share of the sweep; every 1V here turns the phase width knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Carries the number of the active step, 10V divided by the module's step count for each step, and 0V while every step's phase width is 0
Carries the phase of the active step, rising from 0V at the start of the step to 10V at its end
Carries the voltage generated by the active step
Note — the light above each step shows the phase of that step while it is active, running from red at phase 0 to green at phase 1
A sequencer of 4 steps, each generating a curve between two anchor voltages, with its own trigger, interrupt, sustain, shape, curvature and duration settings
Toggles the sequencer between running and paused; a sequence paused this way resumes from where it stopped
While this gate is high the sequencer runs, and while it is low a sequence in progress pauses where it is; it reads high above 1V
Toggles looping; with it on the sequencer begins a new sequence as soon as one ends, and with it off the sequencer goes idle
While this gate is high the sequencer begins a new sequence as soon as one ends; it reads high above 1V
Sets the step the sequence begins at
Sets how many steps the sequence runs for, counting on from the start step and wrapping round to step 1
Sends a gate for as long as it is held: from idle it starts the sequence, and the steps read it for their trigger condition
Starts the sequence when it rises while the sequencer is idle, and the steps read it for their trigger condition; it reads high above 1V
Abandons any paused or running sequence while pressed; the sequencer then starts a new one or goes idle, according to RUN
A rising edge abandons any paused or running sequence; the sequencer then starts a new one or goes idle, according to RUN
Scales every step's anchor LEVEL knob, 0 to 100%

Sets the range of every step's anchor LEVEL knob: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
Multiplies the duration of every step, 0 to 200%; no step is shortened below the minimum of the chosen duration range
Modulates the duration multiplier; every 1V here turns the DUR knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets the range of every step's DUR knob: 1ms to 1 second, 10ms to 10 seconds, or 100ms to 100 seconds, with the knob centred giving a tenth of the maximum
A signal that any step's start or end anchor can sample or track
Carries the number of the active step, 10V divided by the module's step count for each step, and 0V while the sequencer is idle
Carries 10V while the active step is generating its curve, and 0V otherwise
Carries 10V while the active step is sustaining, and 0V otherwise
Carries a 0.9ms 10V pulse each time a step finishes, despite the manual giving the pulse as 10ms
Carries a 0.9ms 10V pulse when the sequence starts or loops, despite the manual giving the pulse as 10ms
Carries the voltage generated by the active step
Chooses what makes that step fire its own trigger: the GATE rising, falling, either rising or falling, being high, or being low
Chooses whether a trigger cuts that step short while it is generating its curve and advances the sequence, or is ignored until the curve finishes
Chooses whether that step holds its end anchor voltage once the curve finishes until a trigger arrives, or advances to the next step straight away
Chooses how that step's start anchor reads its source: SMPL takes one reading when the step starts and holds it, TRACK follows the source for as long as the step runs
Chooses where that step's start anchor takes its voltage: its own LEVEL knob, the A, B or C input, or the OUT jack
Sets the voltage of that step's start anchor while LEVEL is the anchor's chosen source, within the range set by the UNI/BI switch and scaled by the global LEVEL knob
Chooses how that step's end anchor reads its source: SMPL takes one reading when the step starts and holds it, TRACK follows the source for as long as the step runs
Chooses where that step's end anchor takes its voltage: its own LEVEL knob, the A, B or C input, or the OUT jack
Sets the voltage of that step's end anchor while LEVEL is the anchor's chosen source, within the range set by the UNI/BI switch and scaled by the global LEVEL knob

Sets how long that step's curve takes, within the range chosen by the duration range switch and multiplied by the global DUR knob
Enables that step; with it off the sequencer skips the step when advancing
Note — the light above each step shows how far that step has progressed, running from red at the start of its curve to green at the end

lines: Generates one envelope stage: on a trigger it travels from the voltage at IN to the LEVEL voltage over the set duration
Sets the voltage at which the generated stage ends, 0-10V
Sets the curvature of the stage; centred is a straight line, clockwise pushes the steep part towards the end and counter-clockwise towards the start, and the extremes are nearly square
Sets how long the stage takes, 10ms to 10 seconds, with the centre position giving 1 second
While this gate is high the IN signal passes straight to OUT and any stage in progress is abandoned; it reads high above 1V
A rising edge starts a stage from the voltage at IN; a rise during a stage abandons it and starts a new one, and rises are ignored while DEFER is high; it reads high above 1V
The voltage a stage starts from, sampled when the trigger arrives, and passed straight to OUT while DEFER is high
Carries 10V while a stage is being generated or while DEFER is high, and 0V otherwise
Carries a 1ms 10V pulse when a stage completes
Carries the generated stage, the IN voltage while DEFER is high, or the LEVEL voltage after a stage has completed
Note — a knob turned while a stage runs takes effect at once, and the new value applies to the remainder of that stage
A waveshaper that applies a tunable sigmoid transfer function to its input
Sets the curvature of the transfer function; the centre position is a straight line, and the extremes are so steep the curve is nearly square
Chooses the shape of the transfer function: a J curve that steepens at one end, or an S curve that steepens through the middle
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the curvature, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Chooses the signal range the shaper works over: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI. The input is clamped to that range before it is shaped
Modulates the curvature; every 1V here turns the CURVE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
The signal to be shaped, clamped to the chosen range first
The shaped signal, within the chosen range
Note — no anti-aliasing is applied, so shaping an audio signal hard will alias
Swave.notes: No family for the IN and OUT jacks: Swave shapes whatever it is given, audio or modulation, so what those jacks carry depends on the patch.

lines: Two knobs whose output follows an adjustable curve rather than a straight line
Picks a position along that taper's transfer function, which sets the output voltage
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates that taper's level, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates that taper's level; every 1V here turns the LEVEL knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Sets the curvature of that taper; the centre position gives a straight line, turning away from the centre bends the transfer function harder, and counter-clockwise inverts the bend
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates that taper's curvature, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates that taper's curvature; every 1V here turns the CURVE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Chooses the shape of that taper: a J curve that steepens at one end, or an S curve that steepens through the middle
Sets the range of that taper's output: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
Carries that taper's transfer function applied to the position of its LEVEL knob
Note — driving a LEVEL knob past its normal range with control voltage can produce voltages far outside that range, especially with the CURVE knob near either extreme
A truth table with 2 inputs, giving a chosen result for every combination of their states
One of the table's inputs; a voltage above 1V counts as high, despite the manual giving the threshold as 0.5V
The gate input for the table; the gate condition button chooses which condition on it makes the gate column true, and a voltage above 1V counts as high, where the manual says 0.5V
Sets that input high while pressed
Chooses the condition on the gate that makes the gate column true: the gate rises, falls, either rises or falls, is high, or is low. Rise, fall and edge each last a single sample
Chooses the result for that row of the table: T emits 10V, F emits 0V, Q leaves the output as it is, and the fourth setting toggles the output
Carries 10V while the table's result is true and 0V while it is false
Carries the negation of the Q output: 0V while the result is true and 10V while it is false
Forces the result true while pressed, so Q carries 10V and the negated output carries 0V
Forces the result false while pressed, so Q carries 0V and the negated output carries 10V
Note — the toggling result flips the output on every sample its row is selected, so it is worth using only on rows reached through a rise, fall or edge condition
Truth2.notes: The maker's manual says an input above 0.5V counts as high; the 2.0.3 source reads an input as high above 1V. The lines follow the source.

lines: Sets the starting voltage for an envelope and blocks its triggers, for use with the Stage, Booster Stage and Hostage modules
Sets the voltage sent to OUT, within the range chosen by the UNI/BI switch
Sets the range of the LEVEL knob: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
Modulates the level; every 1V here turns the LEVEL knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Blocks triggers from both the TRIG input and the TRIG button while pressed
Raises the TRIG output to 10V while pressed, unless triggers are being blocked
While this gate is high, triggers from both the TRIG input and the TRIG button are blocked; it reads high above 1V
A high signal here raises the TRIG output, unless triggers are being blocked; it reads high above 1V
Carries 10V while the TRIG input is high or the TRIG button is pressed, and 0V while triggers are blocked
Carries the LEVEL voltage, for use as the voltage an envelope starts from
Low frequency oscillator tracing a fixed point on a circle rolling inside or outside another circle, producing a pair of complex pulsing signals at its X and Y outputs
Sets the frequency of the throb cycle, -10 to 10 rotations per second, a negative value running the pattern the other way
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the speed, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the speed; every 1V here turns the SPEED knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Sets how many wobble cycles occur in each throb cycle, over the range chosen by the IN/OUT switch
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the ratio, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the ratio; every 1V here turns the RATIO knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
LOCK rounds the ratio to a whole number, so the pattern of accents repeats on every throb; FREE allows fractional ratios, so the accents vary from one throb to the next
Sets the range of the RATIO knob: 0 to -16 at IN, 0 to 16 at OUT, or -16 to 16 in the middle position, where the RATIO knob chooses the direction of the wobble as well as its rate
Sets how much the wobble cycle dominates the output against the throb cycle, 0 to 100%
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the depth, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the depth; every 1V here turns the DEPTH knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Offsets the phase of the wobble, -180 to 180 degrees, which shifts where the accents fall within each throb
Attenuates and inverts the CV that modulates the phase offset, -100% to 100%, with no effect at the centre position
Modulates the phase offset; every 1V here turns the PHASE knob a tenth of its travel clockwise, after the attenuverter
Scales that output from 0 to 200%, applied after the voltage range is chosen
Modulates the gain of that output; every 1V here turns the GAIN knob a tenth of its travel clockwise
Sets the range of that output: 0-10V at UNI, or -5 to 5V at BI
The horizontal coordinate of the traced point, as a slow pulsing signal
The vertical coordinate of the traced point, as a slow pulsing signal
Note — patching X into a scope's X input and Y into its Y input, with the scope in X times Y mode, draws the rolling-circle shape the module traces
